mainTopic: Setting up a backup wife for the כהן גדול without two 'houses', challenges from יבום, and the כהן גדול who is an אונן
overview: The תורה says the כהן גדול atones on יום הכפורים 'for his house' (ביתו), meaning his wife. ביתו implies one wife, not two and not zero. So the גמרא searches for a way to prepare a backup wife without breaking that rule. It tests several conditional-divorce (גט על תנאי) setups. Each one fails, because it could leave him with two wives or with none. The working setup gives the second wife a גט that depends on the כהן גדול himself entering the בית הכנסת. That way he can act in time if the other wife is about to die. רב אסי then objects that if 'house' means one wife, two widows of one man could never do יבום, and רבינא objects that a ארוסה would be exempt from יבום. Both are answered from extra words in the יבום verses: 'יבמתו' repeated, and 'החוצה'. The גמרא then quotes a ברייתא: a כהן גדול may serve while an אונן but may not eat, and רבי יהודה adds 'כל היום'. רבא explains that this means we bring him from his house to serve. אביי refutes this from רבי יהודה's strict ruling elsewhere, and רבא begins a new explanation that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The previous setup could leave him with two wives
steps.stepSummary: This finishes a challenge begun on the previous amud. If the first wife dies, the second wife's conditional גט turns out to be invalid למפרע, so he did the עבודה while married to two women.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Perhaps the first wife will die, and it will turn out] retroactively that this woman's divorce is not a divorce, and he performed the service with two houses!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes knocking down the previous suggestion, a גט to the second wife on condition that the first wife does not die. If the first wife does die, the second was never divorced, so he was married to two wives during the עבודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is the word למפרע (retroactively). A conditional גט is only decided once we know whether the condition was kept. If the first wife dies in the middle of the day, the second wife's גט is void from the start, so for part of the עבודה he had two wives. That breaks the rule of ביתו, one house and not two.

keyTerms.meaning: Retroactively, looking back from the start
The Temple service of יום הכפורים
With two 'houses', i.e., married to two wives

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the END of an objection that started on the previous amud. It is not a new statement. The earlier condition was 'on condition that your counterpart does NOT die.'

phrases.aramaic: לְמַפְרֵעַ דְּגִיטָּא דְּהָא לָאו גִּיטָּא הוּא,
phrases.english: retroactively, that the divorce of this one is not a divorce,
phrases.notes: This finishes the thought from the previous amud: 'and perhaps the first wife will die and it will turn out...'

phrases.english: and he performed the service with two houses!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the objection begun at the end of the previous amud against the condition 'that your counterpart will not die'.
steps.kashyaTarget: The setup where the second wife is divorced on condition that the first wife does not die
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the condition fails mid-day, the גט is void למפרע, and he was married to two women during the עבודה.

steps.title: Divorce the backup on condition that the first wife dies
steps.stepSummary: New suggestion: the כהן גדול tells the second wife her גט takes effect only if the first wife dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is where he said to her: Here is your divorce, on condition that your counterpart dies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא flips the condition. Now the second wife's גט works only if the first wife dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The aim is that the two wives are never married to him at the same moment. Linking the second wife's divorce to the first wife's death is meant to make sure that when one 'house' leaves, the arrangement switches cleanly. The next step shows why this fails too.

keyTerms.meaning: Here is your bill of divorce (standard formula)

phrases.english: Rather, it is where he said to her:

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה גִּיטֵּיךְ עַל מְנָת שֶׁתָּמוּת חֲבֶרְתִּיךְ.
phrases.english: Here is your divorce, on condition that your counterpart dies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected setup with the opposite condition.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אלא, a new setup)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The backup is divorced on condition that the first wife does NOT die.
steps.terutzMaskana: The backup is divorced on condition that the first wife DOES die.

steps.title: That could leave him with no wife at all
steps.stepSummary: If the first wife dies, the second wife's גט becomes valid, and the כהן גדול is left with no wife (בלא בית).
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps her counterpart will die, and this divorce will be a valid divorce, and he will be left without a house!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the new setup. If the first wife dies, her death triggers the second wife's divorce, so both 'houses' are gone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The backup exists to cover the case where the first wife dies. Under this condition, that very death divorces the backup. He ends up with zero wives, the opposite of what was needed, and he must atone for ביתו.

keyTerms.meaning: Without a house, i.e., with no wife

phrases.english: But perhaps her counterpart will die,
and this one's divorce becomes a valid divorce,
and he is left without a house!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the setup proposed in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The condition 'on condition that your counterpart dies'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first wife's death would divorce the backup too, leaving him with zero wives.

steps.title: Divorce both wives with different conditions
steps.stepSummary: New idea: give both wives conditional גיטין. One works if the other wife does not die. The other works if she does not enter the בית הכנסת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he divorces both of them. To one he says: Here is your divorce on condition that your counterpart does not die. To the other he says: Here is your divorce on condition that you do not enter the synagogue.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a two-sided setup where each wife gets her own conditional גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each condition aims to divorce one wife while keeping the other. Wife A is divorced as long as wife B stays alive. Wife B is divorced if she simply stays out of the בית הכנסת. The next step shows why this can still go wrong.

phrases.english: Rather, he divorces both of them.
To one he says:

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה גִּיטֵּיךְ עַל מְנָת שֶׁלֹּא תָּמוּת חֲבֶרְתִּיךְ,
phrases.english: Here is your divorce, on condition that your counterpart does not die,
and to the other he says:
Here is your divorce, on condition
that you do not enter the synagogue.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the failed one-wife condition with a two-wife arrangement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אלא, a new setup)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the backup wife gets a conditional גט.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both wives get conditional גיטין with different conditions.

steps.title: Both conditions might be kept, leaving no wife
steps.stepSummary: If wife B does not die and also does not enter the בית הכנסת, both גיטין take effect, and he has no wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps her counterpart will not die, and she will not enter the synagogue, and the divorces of both will be valid, and he will be left without a house!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the two-condition setup can collapse. Both conditions can easily be kept at the same time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each condition was meant to work on its own, but nothing stops both from coming true together. Wife B stays alive, which divorces A, and she stays out of the בית הכנסת, which divorces B. The problem is that the women's actions decide the outcome, and he has no control.

phrases.english: But perhaps her counterpart will not die,
and she will not enter the synagogue,
and the divorce of both of them becomes a valid divorce,
and he is left without a house!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the two-condition setup of step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The pairing of 'your counterpart will not die' with 'you will not enter the synagogue'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both conditions can be kept at once, which divorces both wives.

steps.title: The working setup: the second condition depends on the כהן גדול himself
steps.stepSummary: Wife A's גט works on condition that wife B does not die. Wife B's גט works on condition that the כהן גדול enters the בית הכנסת. Whichever wife dies, the other remains married to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, to one he says: Here is your divorce on condition that your counterpart does not die. To the other he says: Here is your divorce on condition that I enter the synagogue. So if this one dies, that one remains; and if that one dies, this one remains.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new setup where the second condition is in the husband's own hands. Now exactly one wife is always his.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If wife A dies, wife B is still married, because her גט only works if he enters the בית הכנסת, and he does not. If wife B dies, wife A's condition (that B not die) fails, so A was never divorced and remains his wife. Either way, exactly one 'house' remains.
steps.whatToRemember: The key move is a condition the כהן גדול controls himself (his entering the בית הכנסת). The women's actions can no longer upset the arrangement.

phrases.english: Rather, to one he says:

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה גִּיטֵּיךְ עַל מְנָת שֶׁלֹּא תָּמוּת חֲבֶרְתִּיךְ.
phrases.english: Here is your divorce, on condition that your counterpart does not die.
And to the other he says:
Here is your divorce, on condition
that I will enter the synagogue.
So if this one dies, that one remains;
and if that one dies, this one remains.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fixes step 5's flaw by switching the second condition from the wife's action to the husband's action.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אלא, a new setup)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The second condition depends on the wife (not entering the synagogue).
steps.terutzMaskana: The second condition depends on the husband (his entering the synagogue), so he controls the outcome.

steps.title: What if wife B dies in the middle of the service?
steps.stepSummary: The possible objection: if wife B dies halfway through the עבודה, wife A's גט becomes void למפרע. That would mean he did part of the עבודה with two wives.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is there to say? Perhaps her counterpart will die in the middle of the service, and it will turn out retroactively that he performed the service with two houses?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises the one remaining worry about the working setup. This sets up the next step, which answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If wife B dies mid-עבודה, wife A's condition (that B not die) has failed, so A was married all along. B was also married until she died. That means two wives during the first half of the עבודה. This is the same למפרע problem as in step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: What is there to say? (raising a possible objection)
In the middle of the service

phrases.english: What is there to say?
Perhaps her counterpart will die in the middle of the service,

phrases.aramaic: וְעָבֵד לֵיהּ עֲבוֹדָה לְמַפְרֵעַ בִּשְׁנֵי בָתִּים?
phrases.english: and retroactively he will have performed the service with two houses?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the setup of step 6 against a timing problem.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A death in the middle of the service makes wife A's גט void למפרע, creating two houses for part of the עבודה.

steps.title: He enters the בית הכנסת in time to divorce the dying wife
steps.stepSummary: If he sees wife B about to die, he quickly enters the בית הכנסת. That makes her גט valid למפרע, so he only ever had one wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he sees that she is about to die, he goes ahead and enters the synagogue, and makes this one's divorce a valid divorce retroactively.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the timing worry. Because the condition is in the כהן גדול's hands, he can act before wife B dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By entering the בית הכנסת, he fulfills wife B's condition, so B counts as divorced from the start. Wife A, whose condition failed through B's death, counts as married from the start. So for the whole day exactly one wife was his, and the למפרע problem is solved.

keyTerms.meaning: He goes ahead early, acts first

steps.whatToRemember: The final solution works because the husband controls one condition and can trigger it at the right moment. This keeps him at exactly one wife for the whole day.

phrases.aramaic: אִי חָזֵי לַהּ דְּקָא בָּעֲיָא לְמֵימַת —
phrases.english: If he sees that she is about to die,
he goes ahead and enters the synagogue,
and makes this one's divorce a valid divorce retroactively.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי חָזֵי לַהּ דְּקָא בָּעֲיָא לְמֵימַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the timing objection of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical solution using the husband's control of the condition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A mid-service death automatically creates two houses למפרע.
steps.terutzMaskana: He fulfills wife B's condition before she dies, so she was divorced from the start and only one wife remains.

steps.title: רב אסי: then two widows from one house could never do יבום
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי (or רב עוירא) objects to the whole idea that 'house' means one wife. If so, two widows of one man (יבמות) could not be taken in יבום, since the יבום verse also speaks of building one 'house'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי, and some say רב עוירא, objected: But if so, two יבמות who come from one house should not undergo יבום!
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge opens against the basic reading of ביתו as 'one wife, not two'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The יבום section says 'who does not build his brother's house', also in the singular. If 'house' means one wife, then when the deceased left two wives, the case would fall outside יבום. Yet we know there is יבום in such a case, so the reading of 'house' seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so (introduces an absurd result)
Widows of a childless man, bound for levirate marriage

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַסִּי, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב עַוִּירָא:
phrases.english: Rav Asi, and some say Rav Avira, objected to this:
But if so,
two yevamot who come from one house,
should not undergo levirate marriage!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַסִּי, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב עַוִּירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the conditional-divorce discussion and challenges its foundation, the reading of 'house' as one wife.
steps.kashyaTarget: The derivation that 'house' (ביתו) means one wife and not two
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same reading applied to 'his brother's house' in יבום would wrongly exclude a case of two widows.

steps.title: The double word "יבמתו" includes the case of two widows
steps.stepSummary: The תורה repeats the word "יבמתו" (his יבמה) twice. This extra word comes to include the case where the deceased left two wives, so יבום applies there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב אסי. The יבום case is covered by a special extra word in the verses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On its own, 'house' would mean one wife in יבום too. But the doubled "יבמתו" is a ריבוי (inclusion) that adds the two-widow case. So the rule of 'one house' stands, and יבום is simply an exception created by the extra word.
steps.whyThisMatters: This keeps the derivation of ביתו as 'one wife' intact, which the whole backup-wife discussion depends on.

phrases.english: "His yevama," "his yevama": the repetition includes [that case].
phrases.notes: The words 'his yevama' show up twice, in דברים 25:7 and 25:9.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אסי's objection from step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Scriptural inclusion (ריבוי) from a repeated word
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'House' in יבום would exclude two widows.
steps.terutzMaskana: The doubled "יבמתו" specifically includes the two-widow case, while 'house' still means one wife elsewhere.

steps.title: If a ארוסה is not 'his house', would she be exempt from יבום?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא (or רב שרביא) challenges the idea that a ארוסה is not counted as a man's 'house'. If that were true, a ארוסה whose betrothed husband died should not need יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא, and some say רב שרביא, objects: If so, a ארוסה should not have יבום?
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge is aimed at the 'house' reasoning. If 'house' only means a fully married wife, a woman who was only betrothed should fall outside יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The יבום passage talks about building the dead brother's 'house' (בית אחיו). If a ארוסה does not count as 'his house', she should not be included in יבום. But we know that a ארוסה does need יבום or חליצה, so the reasoning seems to prove too much.

keyTerms.meaning: He strongly objects to it (a sharp logical challenge)
A betrothed woman: after קידושין but before נישואין

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse ארוסה (betrothed, the first stage) with נשואה (fully married). In Jewish law, a ארוסה is already legally married in many respects, but she has not yet entered her husband's home.

phrases.english: Ravina strongly objects to it,
and some say it was Rav Sherevya:
But if that is so,
should a betrothed woman not undergo levirate marriage?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רָבִינָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב שֵׁרֵבְיָה: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 9. Step 9 attacked the 'one house' reading with two widows. This step attacks the 'house = full wife' reading with a ארוסה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that a ארוסה does not count as a man's 'house'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reductio ad absurdum: the יבום verse also speaks of a 'house'. So if a ארוסה is not 'house', she would be excluded from יבום, and that contradicts known הלכה.

steps.title: The word 'החוצה' includes the ארוסה
steps.stepSummary: The extra word 'החוצה' in the יבום verse comes to include a ארוסה in the law of יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Outside' comes to include the betrothed woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. A special word in the פסוק includes the ארוסה in יבום, even though she is not 'his house'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says 'לא תהיה אשת המת החוצה לאיש זר', and the word 'החוצה' is extra. It teaches that even a woman still 'outside' the home (a ארוסה) is bound to the brother. So the 'house' reasoning stands, and the ארוסה's יבום comes from a separate word, just like the two widows were included through 'יבמתו' in step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Outside': the word from the יבום verse (דברים 25:5)
To include: an extra word widens the law

steps.whatToRemember: Both challenges to the 'house' idea (two widows, and the ארוסה) are answered the same way. A separate extra word in the יבום פסוק includes each case. So 'house' can still mean one fully married wife for the כהן גדול on יום כפור.

phrases.english: "Outside"
phrases.notes: From דברים 25:5: the wife of the dead shall not be married outside to a stranger.

phrases.english: comes to include the betrothed woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the קשיא of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Separate scriptural inclusion (ריבוי) from an extra word
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a ארוסה is not 'house', she would seem to be outside יבום.
steps.terutzMaskana: A ארוסה is included in יבום through 'החוצה', so the 'house' reasoning does not need to change.

steps.title: A כהן גדול may offer קרבנות as an אונן but not eat
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a כהן גדול who is an אונן may bring קרבנות but may not eat from them. רבי יהודה adds the words 'כל היום'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A כהן גדול offers sacrifices as an אונן but does not eat. רבי יהודה says: the entire day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic, related to the earlier case of the כהן גדול's wife dying. It quotes a ברייתא about a כהן גדול who is in early mourning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אונן is someone whose close relative died that day. A regular כהן may not serve then, but a כהן גדול may. Even so, he may not eat קדשים. רבי יהודה's short addition, 'כל היום', is unclear, and that sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A mourner on the day a close relative died, before burial
Offers or performs the קרבן service

steps.whyThisMatters: It connects to the earlier case. If the כהן גדול's wife dies on יום כפור, he becomes an אונן. This ברייתא tells us he can still serve.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A High Priest sacrifices as an acute mourner,
but does not eat.
Rabbi Yehuda says: the entire day.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל מַקְרִיב אוֹנֵן, וְאֵינוֹ אוֹכֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ברייתא, brought in because the earlier sugya discussed the death of the כהן גדול's wife.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן גדול may serve while an אונן but may not eat קדשים. רבי יהודה adds 'כל היום'.

steps.title: What does 'the entire day' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי יהודה's phrase 'כל היום' adds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about רבי יהודה's words. This sets up the explanations that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'כל היום' is too short to understand on its own. It could change what he may do, when he may do it, or how. The גמרא needs to define it before going further.

phrases.english: What is "the entire day"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of רבי יהודה's addition in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does רבי יהודה's phrase 'כל היום' come to teach?

steps.title: רבא: we even bring him from his house to serve
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that 'כל היום' teaches that we actively bring the mourning כהן גדול from his house to serve in the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is needed only to bring him from his house.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a first answer. רבי יהודה means the כהן גדול is not only allowed to serve; we even fetch him from home to serve.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of the ברייתא only allows service if he is already in the מקדש. According to רבא, רבי יהודה goes further: he is brought in from home, perhaps to ease his pain. So 'כל היום' widens the permission into an active encouragement.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed only for: points to the exact new point
To bring him from inside his house

phrases.english: Rava said:
It is necessary only
to bring him from his house.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לַהֲבִיאוֹ מִתּוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'כל היום' means the mourning כהן גדול is brought from his house to serve.

steps.title: אביי: רבי יהודה actually sends a mourning priest out
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבא from another ברייתא. There, רבי יהודה rules that a כהן who hears of a relative's death in the middle of his service leaves at once. How then could רבי יהודה say we bring a mourner in from his house?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Now, according to רבי יהודה we remove him, as it was taught: If he was standing and offering on the altar and heard that a relative died, he leaves his service and goes out. These are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי יוסי says: He should finish. And you say we bring him from his house?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבא's explanation. He shows that רבי יהודה is actually strict about a mourner serving.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the other ברייתא, רבי יהודה makes a כהן stop in the middle of his service. רבי יוסי lets him finish. If רבי יהודה removes a mourner who is already at the מזבח, it makes no sense that he would bring one in from home. So רבא's reading of 'כל היום' contradicts רבי יהודה's own view.

keyTerms.meaning: Now (introduces a contradiction: 'now, if he holds X, how can you say Y?')

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא about leaving the service speaks of a regular כהן. אביי assumes רבי יהודה's strict view applies to a כהן גדול too. That assumption is what makes the challenge work.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Now, according to Rabbi Yehuda,
we actually remove him, as it was taught:
If he was standing and sacrificing
on top of the altar
and heard that a relative of his died,
he leaves his service and goes out;
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Yosei says: He should finish.
And you say
we bring him from his house?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: הַשְׁתָּא לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַפּוֹקֵי מַפְּקִינַן לֵיהּ
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reading that רבי יהודה brings the mourning כהן גדול from his house.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Contradiction with רבי יהודה's own ruling elsewhere. He removes a mourning כהן even in the middle of service, so he would never bring one in from home.

steps.title: רבא withdraws and begins a new explanation
steps.stepSummary: רבא drops his first explanation and starts again with the question of what 'כל היום' means. His new answer comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: What is 'the entire day'?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. רבא accepts אביי's challenge and gets ready to give a new meaning for 'כל היום'. The answer itself continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אלא' shows that the first explanation is withdrawn. רבא reopens the same question, so his new answer must fit רבי יהודה's strict view about a mourning כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: rejects what came before and starts a new answer

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
What is "the entire day"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to אביי's קשיא in step 16 by dropping the first explanation and starting a second one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Retraction and reinterpretation (the new answer continues on the next amud)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'כל היום' means we bring him from his house.
steps.terutzMaskana: That reading is rejected. A new meaning of 'כל היום' is about to be given.
